theory.heading: Follow written dimensions
theory.body: Written dimensions control the intended size of a feature. They are more reliable than estimating from the apparent length of a line or measuring a picture on a screen. A preview can change size because of zoom, display settings or cropping, so it must never be treated as a measuring surface. Use the unchanged original two-page Footstool drawing as the dimensional authority. When information appears unclear or conflicting elsewhere, return to the original drawing and seek clarification rather than selecting or inventing a value.

theory.heading: Read symbols as communication cues
theory.body: Technical drawings use symbols, line types, labels and notes to communicate information efficiently. A symbol is a cue that directs the reader to a particular meaning, such as the type of feature or how written information should be interpreted. It should be read with the nearby view, dimension or note rather than in isolation. Do not assume that a familiar-looking symbol has the same meaning in every situation. Identify where it appears, connect it to the relevant feature and use the teacher-provided drawing guidance when interpretation is uncertain.

theory.heading: Understand scale proportionally
theory.body: Scale describes a proportional relationship between the drawing and the intended object. A scaled drawing may be smaller or larger than the actual product while keeping its parts in consistent proportion. Scale helps a drawing fit clearly on a page, but it does not make screen measurements reliable. Written dimensions still control intended size. A sound drawing check asks whether the correct original page is being used, whether the symbol or note is linked to the right feature and whether the written dimension has been read directly. Current school SOPs and teacher directions control all actual workshop activity.

questions.question: What controls the intended size of a feature on the Footstool drawing?
choices: The apparent length of the line
questions.correctFeedback: Correct. Written dimensions control intended size and are more reliable than visual estimates.
questions.retryFeedback: Review Follow written dimensions and focus on which information controls intended size.

questions.question: Why must a screen preview never be measured?
choices: Its displayed size can change with zoom or cropping
It always shows a different product
questions.correctFeedback: Correct. Zoom, display settings and cropping can change the apparent size of a screen preview.
questions.retryFeedback: Return to Follow written dimensions and identify why a preview is not a reliable measuring surface.

questions.question: What should a student do when dimensional information conflicts with another classroom example?
choices: Choose the value that looks more suitable
Return to the original drawing and seek clarification
questions.correctFeedback: Correct. The original two-page drawing remains the dimensional authority, and uncertainty should be clarified.
questions.retryFeedback: Re-read Follow written dimensions and focus on the response to unclear or conflicting information.

questions.question: What is the broad purpose of symbols on a technical drawing?
choices: To show the drawing is complete
questions.correctFeedback: Correct. Symbols communicate meaning efficiently and guide the reader towards relevant information.
questions.retryFeedback: Review Read symbols as communication cues and locate the explanation of what symbols do.

questions.question: How should a drawing symbol be interpreted?
choices: By guessing from its shape alone
By reading it with the nearby view, note or dimension
By applying it to every feature
questions.correctFeedback: Correct. A symbol gains meaning from its connection to the relevant feature and nearby information.
questions.retryFeedback: Return to Read symbols as communication cues and focus on what should be read together.

questions.question: What should a student do when the meaning of a symbol is uncertain?
choices: Use the drawing guidance and ask for clarification
questions.correctFeedback: Correct. Approved guidance and clarification prevent unsupported interpretations.
questions.retryFeedback: Re-read Read symbols as communication cues and identify the response to uncertainty.

questions.question: What does drawing scale describe?
choices: The proportional relationship between drawing and object
questions.correctFeedback: Correct. Scale describes how drawing size relates proportionally to the intended object.
questions.retryFeedback: Review Understand scale proportionally and focus on the opening definition.

questions.question: Why might a technical drawing use scale?
choices: To fit the product clearly on a page while preserving proportion
To remove the need for dimensions
questions.correctFeedback: Correct. Scale allows a product to be represented clearly while keeping parts in consistent proportion.
questions.retryFeedback: Return to Understand scale proportionally and identify why scale is useful.

questions.question: Which information still controls intended size on a scaled drawing?
questions.correctFeedback: Correct. Written dimensions remain the controlling size information even when a drawing is scaled.
questions.retryFeedback: Re-read Understand scale proportionally and focus on what scale does not replace.

questions.question: Which check best supports accurate drawing interpretation?
choices: Measure the preview and compare it with memory
Apply every note to every view
Use the correct original page, link symbols to features and read written dimensions directly
questions.correctFeedback: Correct. Accurate interpretation combines the authoritative page, correctly linked cues and directly read dimensions.
questions.retryFeedback: Review the final sentences of Understand scale proportionally and identify all parts of the drawing check.

written.prompt: Explain how written dimensions, symbols and scale work together when reading a technical drawing, including why a screen preview must not be measured.
written.sentenceStarter: Written dimensions control ___, symbols help communicate ___, and scale shows ___. A screen preview must not be measured because ___.
written.example: Written dimensions control intended size, symbols help communicate feature information, and scale shows the proportional relationship between the drawing and object. A screen preview must not be measured because its displayed size can change.
